title: intent claude rules index gets clap's unknown-subcommand error at exit 1, not the retired refusal at exit 2
body:
`intent claude rules index` was a shipped spelling in v3.0.3 (it answered "is a known command that is not implemented yet") and was deleted in d843f7aea. It has no row in the dispatch table's `retired` population, so 3.1.0 answers it with clap's generic `error: unrecognized subcommand 'index'` at exit 1, not the "was retired in Intent v3" refusal at exit 2 that `claude ws`, which was withdrawn the same way, gets (driven on 3.1.0 under an isolated HOME: `claude ws list` exits 2 naming `intent wb register`; `claude rules index` exits 1).

Fix: a `retire` row for it, or a ruling that a withdrawn unimplemented spelling does not need one. XS. Found in dc's doc sweep of 2026-09-18.



CLOSED 2026-09-19, by the landing at fb80369ab on vc's GO (T1, patch-id d5f451ba35dd, judged green at f46411fd7: intentsvcs 1804 passed 0 failed, intent-cli 1034 passed 0 failed). vc ruled the retire row. `claude rules index` has a row of its own in surface/dispatch-table.json, state and disposition `retire`, with an empty spelling because the binary serves the rule library and there is no index file to regenerate. The retire/retire census moved from 14 to 15. Driven on the worktree build: it exits 2 with "`intent claude rules index` was retired in Intent v3 and is not a command in this build", where 3.1.0 exited 1 with clap's `unrecognized subcommand`. retired_commands.rs covers the row from the table.
